name: tsa_loginByPhone
description: TEMPORARY OTP bypass: looks up an Active worker by phone number and opens a 90-day TSA.Session with no verification. The header says to use it only while SMS is unavailable and to replace the caller with tsa_validateOtp + tsa_createReturnSession once Twilio is provisioned (tsa-eats/app/api/auth/send-otp/route.ts carries the matching TODO). Live as the app's login path. Called by the TSA Eats Next.js app (tsa-eats/lib/api.ts) through api/Endpoints/TsaApi.cs, which maps queryType 'loginByPhone' to [TSA].[tsa_loginByPhone]. There is no Harrier Central auth: POST requires the shared X-Api-Key (TsaApiKey); GET requires nothing, and the shim does not restrict which procedure a GET may name. The shim turns any one-row rowset with Success = 0 into HTTP 400 {success:false, errorMessage}, and an empty first rowset into HTTP 404.

parameters.name: phoneNumber
parameters.description: Phone number in E.164. No default.

rowsets.name: LoginResult
rowsets.description: Always one row of the same six columns: success, not found (line 37), or CATCH (line 53).

columns.name: ErrorMessage
columns.description: NULL on success; 'No active account found for that phone number.' or ERROR_MESSAGE().

sideEffects: INSERT TSA.Session (one row, expiresAt = now + 90 days).

codeSmells.detail: @phoneNumber (line 2) have no SQL default. A caller that omits one is refused by SQL Server before the body runs: no log row, and the TsaApi shim returns a generic 500.
The CATCH (lines 51-55) returns the error envelope but writes nothing to HC.ErrorLog or any TSA log table, so failures are only visible in Azure Function logs as a 400 warning.

codeSmells.issue: Session for anyone who knows a phone number
codeSmells.detail: A 90-day session is issued on phone number alone. Through the shim's unauthenticated GET route (no X-Api-Key) anyone can call GET /api/TsaApi?queryType=loginByPhone&phoneNumber=... and receive a sessionId for any registered officer, and the 'not found' message confirms which numbers are registered.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
